name: pixel-flow-field

frames.best_why: The full word is settled and sharply readable, which the earlier loose-particle frames are not.

tagline: Tiny squares swirl into a blocky word, then scatter away from the pointer.
summary: A dark canvas tiled with thousands of small square cells that drift along a noise flow, gather into a heavy word, and get shoved aside in a fading wake wherever the pointer moves.
appearance: A near-black stage covered in a faint grid of tiny squares. Settled, the squares clump into a thick sans word, FLOW, drawn from visible dots, with a dim speckle of cells spread over the rest of the surface.
behaviour: On arrival the dots float loose and scattered; within a couple of seconds they ease into the letterforms. Moving the pointer pushes nearby cells outward along the drag, leaving a temporary gap in the word that fills back in afterwards.
demo_content: The single word "FLOW" in a very heavy weight.
search_phrases: word made of tiny squares that scatter
dots that form text and run from the cursor
blocky lettering built from small cells
grid of dots rearranging into a word
mouse disturbs letters made of dots
canvas word that breaks apart and reforms
animated dotted logotype for a hero
use_when: A hero or section title should feel computational and react to the pointer while staying readable at rest.
avoid_when: It samples one short word: longer text shrinks until letters stop reading, and the loop runs whenever it is on screen.
customise: Set the word with text, or point src at a CORS-readable image; cellSize, gap, shape, speed, pointer radius and strength, colors and scatter are props.
weight_why: Every visible frame draws up to 14,000 cells on a 2D canvas.

a11y.note: The canvas is hidden from assistive tech and there is nothing to operate; reduced motion freezes one resolved frame.

issues: Frame 1 is a loose starfield with no word, so the first impression does not show what it becomes.
polish_why: Crisp cell-built lettering and a convincing pointer wake; the resting canvas is sparse.
